terms.meaning: a web address that other programs can call to ask the app for something
a group of routes that is attached to the main web app
sending results piece by piece as they are produced, rather than all at once at the end
a library that checks incoming data has the expected shape before the code uses it

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Nothing runs for users here. It loads the web framework, the four agent classes, and the settings, then creates the router and a logger for recording messages.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the file the tools and the router that the routes attach to.

sections.name: CompanyResearchRequest
sections.title: Request shape for company research
sections.what: Describes what a caller must send to ask for company research: the company name, its industry, and an optional list of topics to look into.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the server reject incomplete requests before any research work starts.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a field here causes callers that still use the old name to get an error.

sections.name: IndustryBenchmarkRequest
sections.title: Request shape for industry benchmarks
sections.what: Describes a request for industry benchmark figures: an industry name and an optional list of the measures wanted.
sections.why: Likely reason: same purpose as the other request shapes, so the server knows what to expect.
sections.watch_out: The industry name is free text, so spelling differences can produce different results.

sections.name: ModelAnalysisRequest
sections.title: Request shape for model analysis
sections.what: Describes a request to analyze a company's model: company name, industry, a free-form set of inputs, and optional research data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the inputs are free-form so the analysis can accept different kinds of model data.
sections.watch_out: Because inputs are not checked by name here, missing values are left for the reasoning agent to handle.

sections.name: BenchmarkComparisonRequest
sections.title: Request shape for benchmark comparison
sections.what: Describes a request to compare a company's measures with industry figures: industry, measures as numbers, and optional research data.
sections.why: Likely reason: the measures are numbers so they can be compared directly with benchmarks.
sections.watch_out: Text values in the measures will be rejected by the server before the comparison runs.

sections.name: research_company
sections.title: One-shot company research
sections.what: Runs company research once and returns the complete findings, sources and reasoning log in a single reply. If the research fails, the caller gets a server error that includes the error text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the simple version for callers that do not need live progress updates.
sections.watch_out: The raw error text is sent back to the caller, which can reveal internal details.

sections.name: research_industry_benchmarks
sections.title: One-shot industry benchmark research
sections.what: Asks the research agent to look up industry benchmark figures and returns them with their sources.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The code does not check that the figures are current; the quality depends on what the agent finds.

sections.name: analyze_model
sections.title: One-shot model analysis
sections.what: Sends the company's model inputs to the reasoning agent and returns its analysis with a step-by-step reasoning log.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Input values are passed through without checks, so bad inputs produce bad analysis without any warning.

sections.name: compare_benchmarks
sections.title: Benchmark comparison
sections.what: Compares the company's measures with industry benchmarks and returns an explained comparison.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The usefulness of the comparison depends entirely on the agent and the research data supplied.

sections.name: research_company_stream (part 1)
sections.title: Live research progress stream
sections.what: Sends progress messages while research runs, then the research log, then the final result. The progress steps are sent before the real research starts, so the progress is largely cosmetic.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the interface show activity during a long wait. The code comments say the agent work is not truly asynchronous.
sections.watch_out: The research call blocks the server while it runs, so other requests may stall until it finishes.

sections.name: research_company_stream (part 2)
sections.title: End of research stream code
sections.what: Only a blank line. It has no behavior of its own.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: analyze_model_stream
sections.title: Live model analysis stream
sections.what: Runs the model analysis, then sends its log entries, reasoning steps and final result as a stream. The analysis finishes before streaming starts, so the stream replays finished work.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the interface show results in order without changing the agent code.
sections.watch_out: An error is sent inside the stream while the web status still shows success, so the caller must read the message.

sections.name: get_agent_status (part 1)
sections.title: Provider status check, part one
sections.what: Checks whether the Ollama service answers and lists its models. Checks whether an OpenAI key is set and the client can be created.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the settings screen show which AI providers can be used.
sections.watch_out: OpenAI is reported as available when a key exists. The key is not tested with a real request.

sections.name: get_agent_status (part 2)
sections.title: Provider status check, part two
sections.what: Reports Tavily search as available when its key is set and its library loads, then returns the full status summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: same purpose as the earlier checks, so the screen can show every provider in one reply.
sections.watch_out: A wrong key is still reported as available, because no test call is made.

sections.name: QuestionnaireRequest
sections.title: Request shape for starting questions
sections.what: Describes a request to start the questionnaire: a company name and an optional short description.
sections.why: Likely reason: the first step of the question-and-answer process.
sections.watch_out: The description is optional, so the questions may be generic when it is left out.

sections.name: AnswersRequest
sections.title: Request shape for answers
sections.what: Describes a request carrying the question and answer pairs the user has given.
sections.why: Likely reason: the answers are sent back as text pairs so the agent can classify the company.
sections.watch_out: Only text is accepted, so any numeric answers must be sent as text.

sections.name: ComparablesRequest
sections.title: Request shape for finding comparables
sections.what: Describes a request to find similar public companies: company name, industry, business model, and how many to find (default 5).
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The number requested is not capped here, so a very large number could make the search slow.

sections.name: generate_questions
sections.title: Starting discovery questions
sections.what: Asks the questionnaire agent to produce the first set of discovery questions for a company.
sections.why: Likely reason: starts the interview the user answers before modeling.
sections.watch_out: Errors are returned as server errors with the error text.

sections.name: analyze_answers
sections.title: Classifying the company from answers
sections.what: Sends the answers to the questionnaire agent, which returns an industry classification and a suggested modeling approach.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The classification is only as good as the answers the user gave.

sections.name: find_comparables
sections.title: Finding comparable companies
sections.what: Asks the comparables agent to find similar listed companies, with reasons, up to the number requested.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The search depends on web search results, which may be incomplete or outdated.

sections.name: analyze_comparables
sections.title: Analyzing comparable companies
sections.what: Takes a list of comparable companies and returns financial analysis for each, with sources.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The body must be a plain list of text pairs; a longer list means a longer wait.

sections.name: synthesize_benchmarks
sections.title: Building industry benchmarks from comparables
sections.what: Combines the analyses of several comparable companies into benchmark ranges with statistics.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It expects the output of the earlier analysis step, so callers must pass that output back unchanged.

sections.name: InputsRequest
sections.title: Request shape for required inputs
sections.what: Describes a request carrying a company classification and its context, both as free-form dictionaries.
sections.why: Likely reason: the structure of the classification can vary, so it is accepted loosely.
sections.watch_out: Nothing checks the dictionary shape, so a wrong structure is only caught later, if at all.

sections.name: determine_inputs
sections.title: Determining required financial inputs
sections.what: Given the company's classification, returns the financial inputs the user must supply, with guidance on each.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Depends on the classification having the expected fields; the code does not confirm this.

summary: Defines the web routes that let the app ask AI agents to research companies, benchmark industries, analyze models, and suggest inputs, with some results streamed back as they are produced.
purpose: Exposes the agent features to the front end or other programs. Based on the outline, it covers company research, industry benchmarks, model analysis, questionnaires, comparables, and input suggestions.
why: Likely reason: keeps the web interface separate from the agent logic in the other modules.
how: Only the setup part was read. From the outline, the file defines request shapes for each feature and then the routes that use them. Some routes have streaming versions.
inputs: Request bodies defined in the outline, such as company research, industry benchmark, model analysis, benchmark comparison, questionnaire, answers, comparables, and inputs requests.
outputs: Not visible in the part read. The outline suggests normal responses and streamed responses.
risks: Not visible in the part read. The routes, their error handling, and what they return were not read.
debug: Not visible in the part read. Start by checking the imports, the router, and the agent classes that the routes call.
